title: Closure of bounded-width CNFs under conjunction
statement: Fix $n$ and a width bound $\ell$, and let $f_1, \dots, f_k$ be Boolean functions on $n$ variables, each mapping an assignment $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ to a truth value. Suppose that every $f_i$ is computed by some CNF formula of width at most $\ell$, that is, a conjunction of clauses in which each clause has at most $\ell$ literals. Then their conjunction $x \mapsto \bigwedge_{i=1}^{k} f_i(x)$ is also computed by a single CNF formula of width at most $\ell$.

replaced:
Let an AND gate have a list of children, each of which computes a function expressible
by a CNF of width at most $\ell$. Then the AND of all children is itself computed by a
single CNF of width at most $\ell$, namely the concatenation of the children's clause
lists. This collapses the AND layer and the CNF layer into one.
